title: nonblocking-io-prefetch-interaction-benchmark-and-kernel-saturation-mapper
author: Morgan Patel
description: Add a focused benchmark that exercises the interaction between nonblocking I/O (async client libraries) and our prefetching heuristics, plus a lightweight kernel-saturation mapper that samples kernel occupancy during runs. Motivation: several internal investigations (ENG-2897) showed amplified tail latency when prefetch policies and nonblocking request patterns intersected under high concurrency. This PR delivers: 1) a new runner (benchmarks/io_prefetch/nbio_replay.py) that can replay real session traces with configurable async client concurrency, socket batching windows, and prefetch policy toggles, 2) an epochal kernel sampler (reporters/kernel_saturation_mapper.go) that attaches to running instances to sample per-kernel occupancy and queueing metrics every 50ms, 3) a small operator to correlate kernel saturation with batch sizes and latency histograms (tools/analysis/prefetch_correlation.py), 4) test harness changes to add a dedicated perf CI job (ci/perf/nbio-prefetch.yaml) that runs the benchmark in a reproducible dockerized environment. The description below contains the checklist and usage notes. Checklist: - [x] implement runner + mapper - [x] add unit tests for runner input parsing (benchmarks/io_prefetch/tests) - [x] add integration test that runs a short replay on CI (ci/perf/nbio-prefetch.yaml) - [x] document config knobs and expected outputs (docs/benchmark-lab/nbio-prefetch.md) - [x] add example visualizer script (tools/analysis/prefetch_correlation.py) Usage: run `python nbio_replay.py --trace traces/session_2025-10-01.json --concurrency 128 --prefetch=adaptive --sample-kernel=unix:/tmp/ksock` to execute a 5-minute smoke run that emits CSVs consumed by the mapper. Test plan: local smoke runs, CI perf job for regression signal, and a scheduled nightly job that collects stable baselines. Expected outcome: identify regimes where prefetching increases p99 by >15% when nonblocking clients interleave small sequences. Related: ENG-2922 for follow-up remediation (adaptive backpressure), and a doc describing potential mitigations is linked in the PR.

release_notes: Added a nonblocking I/O vs prefetch interaction benchmark and a kernel saturation mapper to help correlate kernel occupancy with latency under async workloads. Useful for diagnosing prefetch-config-induced tail amplification.
notes: This PR intentionally keeps the kernel sampler lightweight (CSV sink) to avoid heavy instrumentation in the hot path.
Nightly baselines will be created the week after merge; engineering will monitor p95/p99 shifts and open follow-ups if thresholds are breached.
Follow-up work: implement adaptive backpressure in prefetch (ENG-2922) and add GPU-side queueing telemetry ingestion.
